messages.content: The flights are done, so I want to settle the resort now. Please compare the three Rio Grande options for the full seven nights, not just the headline nightly rates.

I’ll price February 21-28 for two adults and separate room charges, taxes, resort fees, parking, and deposits. I’ll also verify the refundable terms, what the Hyatt breakfast-and-credit package actually includes, and whether the quoted room categories remain available.

For hotel rooms, I prefer having both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge. Keep those in the comparison, but tell me if an otherwise strong option is missing one rather than dropping it without discussion.
Understood. I’ll treat both as useful room-level criteria and flag any gap. I’ll also distinguish a usable refrigerator from a stocked minibar or cooler, since those are not necessarily equivalent.
What are the real totals? Assume we will have a rental car at the resort for all seven nights.

The current refundable quotes are: Hyatt Regency Grand Reserve, Ocean View King with breakfast and resort credit, $4,060 room, $385 resort fee, and $740.84 taxes and fee taxes, for $5,185.84 total. Self-parking is included. Wyndham Grand Rio Mar, Ocean View King, $3,675 room, $420 resort fee, $245 self-parking, and $700.18 taxes, for $5,040.18 total. The quieter St. Regis Bahia Beach, Deluxe Oceanfront King, is $5,110 room, $455 destination fee, $315 valet parking, and $963.90 taxes, for $6,843.90 total. None of those totals includes spa treatments.
So the Wyndham is only about $146 less than the Hyatt after everything? Check that arithmetic and the deposits.

Correct. The difference is $145.66 for the seven-night stay. Hyatt requires a $1,481.67 deposit at booking, equal to two nights with associated taxes and fees; the balance is charged at checkout. Wyndham requires $702.89, equal to the first night with taxes, resort fee, and parking. St. Regis requires $1,955.40, equal to two nights plus associated charges. Each deposit is applied to the final bill rather than added to the quoted total.
Now give me the cancellation deadlines precisely. I do not want a vague three-days-before description.

Hyatt permits cancellation without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time on Saturday, February 7, 2026. Beginning February 8, the $1,481.67 deposit is nonrefundable. Wyndham permits cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time on Saturday, February 14; after that, it charges the first-night amount of $702.89. St. Regis permits cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time on Wednesday, February 11; a later cancellation forfeits $1,955.40. A no-show at any property can trigger the same stated penalty and release the remaining nights.
What exactly does the Hyatt package cover? Breakfast offers and resort credits often sound better than they are.

The Hyatt offer includes the breakfast buffet for two registered adults each morning at Water’s Edge from February 22 through February 28. It covers the buffet and applicable tax, but not alcohol, room-service delivery, or gratuity. The $100 resort credit is once per stay, not per day. It can be used for eligible resort dining or spa charges posted to the room, but not toward the room rate, resort fee, taxes, parking, retail purchases, or outside operators. Any unused amount expires at checkout, and charges above $100 remain payable.
Does the credit apply to massages, and are there actually two appointments Monday or Tuesday afternoon? We need separate massages, not a couples treatment.

The credit can be applied to Hyatt spa services charged to the room. The spa currently has two separate 50-minute custom massages available Tuesday, February 24, at 2:00 p.m. with different therapists. Monday has only one appointment at 3:30 p.m., so it cannot accommodate both of you separately at the same time. Tuesday’s two treatments are $185 each, plus a 20% service charge, for $444 total before applying the $100 resort credit.
And the quieter St. Regis? I want to understand what the extra money buys before deciding.

St. Regis can confirm two separate 60-minute massages Monday, February 23, at 2:30 p.m. Its room category is in a lower-density section of the property, and the quoted total includes beach service and nonmotorized water activities through the destination fee. Breakfast is not included. The spa treatments would add $610 including service charges. The room has a coffee machine, but its chilled unit is a stocked minibar intended for hotel products; the property will not confirm it as a guest-use refrigerator. They can request an empty medical refrigerator, but they will not guarantee one for general food storage.
That makes St. Regis less compelling at nearly $1,658 more than Hyatt before the pricier spa. What about the room details and availability at Hyatt and Wyndham?

Hyatt currently has an Ocean View King available for all seven consecutive nights under the refundable breakfast-and-credit rate. The room has a single king bed, furnished balcony, standard in-room coffee maker, and empty mini-fridge. Wyndham also has an Ocean View King for all seven nights, with a balcony, single-serve coffee maker, and empty compact refrigerator. At both properties, “ocean view” is a view category rather than an oceanfront guarantee, and neither quote requires changing rooms mid-stay.
Is the Hyatt total fixed enough to book, or are there any charges still hiding outside it besides spa and ordinary personal spending?

For the stated occupancy and one rental car, $5,185.84 is the complete lodging total currently presented by Hyatt, including room, resort fee, all listed taxes, and self-parking. The booking disclosure allows government tax changes before checkout, and incidental authorization is separate, but there is no additional mandatory property charge in the rate terms. Spa, gratuities, meals beyond the included breakfast, and other personal charges would be extra.
The Hyatt seems like the best value. Before you reserve it, confirm that the $100 credit can reduce the Tuesday massages even though they are booked separately.

Confirmed. Both massage charges may be posted to the same guest room, and the single $100 stay credit will be applied against the combined eligible spa charges. Separate treatment rooms and therapists do not affect eligibility. The spa appointments are not included automatically with the room and need their own reservation.

Book the Hyatt Ocean View King on that refundable breakfast-and-credit rate for February 21-28 at $5,185.84. Use the deposit terms you stated. Also reserve both Tuesday 2:00 p.m. massages and apply the resort credit to the spa bill. Do not book St. Regis or Wyndham.

I have reserved the Hyatt Regency Grand Reserve Puerto Rico Ocean View King for two adults, checking in Saturday, February 21 and checking out Saturday, February 28. The confirmed lodging total is $5,185.84, and $1,481.67 was charged as the deposit; the remaining $3,704.17 is due at the property, subject only to a government-imposed tax change or added personal charges. Cancellation is penalty-free through 11:59 p.m. AST on February 7, 2026; from February 8, the deposit is forfeited. The package includes the daily breakfast buffet for two and one $100 eligible dining-or-spa credit. I also reserved two separate 50-minute custom massages for Tuesday, February 24 at 2:00 p.m., totaling $444 including service charges before the credit. Both will be posted to the room so the $100 credit can reduce the spa balance to $344. Wyndham and St. Regis were not booked. Private airport transfers and the El Yunque outing remain unbooked.
